inputs: HANDOFF.md open items 1, 3, 8, 12 and the round-8 disproof list
outputs: MECHANISM, exact: the mid-range reconstruction branch in the terrain fragment shader is arithmetically dead. Its gate was 'coreFar = core * smoothstep(55,240,dist) * kgNearGrain'; kgNearGrain = 1 - smoothstep(34,78,dist), so the product's maximum over ALL distances is 0.001887 at 67 m, against its own 'if (coreFar > 0.002)' guard. The branch has never executed for a single pixel in any frame this project has captured. It left 45-90 m of core ground carrying nothing but mipped library texture and the 12-48 m nB field.

CORROBORATION in the frame: ray-marching the wide pose (verified below) puts the critic's plateau box at 19-117 m. Measured along it in phone-wide-r15, ground-only strips give dist 25.9 m detail 6.20 / lumaSpread 57.4; 33.3 m 7.31 / 58.7; 39.8 m 6.91 / 50.9; 49.7 m 5.84 / 46.9; 66.7 m 5.36 / 42.2. Detail and spread fall monotonically exactly where kgNearGrain fades and nothing takes over.

FIX A: replaced the dead block with a live 'coreMid' band, core * smoothstep(30,62,dist) * (1 - smoothstep(155,330,dist)), carrying a new footprint-locked octave 'kgMidBand' locked to ~12 drawing-buffer pixels (the existing kgLodBand is locked to ~4). Value applied in debiased stops (1.45 * mid, debias 0.0294*g^2 as the far range uses), then a dry/damp hue split matching the near mottle's character so the cadence is continuous while the scale is zoned. Active over >=31.6% of the wide frame at mean weight 0.608.

FIX B: authored the worn side route the level geometry already implies. Level._buildBridge takes its bearing from LAYOUT.arena -> LAYOUT.overlook and lays a 7.5 m span on it, and _buildOverlook puts a railed terrace at its end; the ground under that route was never worn. Splat only, never carved. Measured on the real CPU pipeline run offline: mean wear over the visible plateau 0.0035 -> 0.0188 (5.4x), gravel 0.1497 -> 0.1549, grass 0.5784 -> 0.5722; 11.6% of the farright probe box's world footprint now carries wear > 0.10, and the route projects across the frame from px 1523 to 2243 at py 702-740, 48-57 m out, crossing the critic's own box.

FIX C: added Terrain.coverAt(x,z), the splat's continuous turf weight, bilinear. surfaceAt collapses five continuous weights to one of five names and 83.9% of the visible plateau returns the single name 'grass'; the weight underneath is mean 0.613, sd 0.260, p10 0.039 against p90 0.888. Foliage._siteWeight reads the name, so it plants a 23:1 density range at one density. That is the mechanism behind the finding's 'uniform stochastic density, no clumping, no drift, no density gradient', it is not fixable from Foliage without an accessor Foliage may not add to this file, and it is now one call away.

DISPROOF, target (a) pctAbove240 >= 0.05%: not reachable from Terrain.js. HANDOFF open item 8 already records that wide is front-lit by construction (sun 123 deg off the view axis, no specular in frame reflects toward the viewer) and is exempt from the highlight gate for that reason. Terrain albedo cannot manufacture a clean highlight in a frame with no specular return.

DISPROOF, target (a) pctBelow16 >= 3.0%: not reachable from Terrain.js. It needs ~74,061 more pixels under luma 16. In the mid-range strip the fix acts on (rows 660-830, 40-100 m) only 3.68% of pixels are even below luma 32 and 0.01% below 16, so halving that band's albedo yields order 1,000 pixels. The near strip (rows 900-1170) holds 1.34% below 16 and 31.9% below 32; hero reaches 8.279% and torii 9.432% from deep prop shadow at close range, which is lighting and composition, not ground albedo.

APPARATUS PASS, measurement harness: the reading script uses tools/probe.mjs's own region/stats and tools/luma.mjs's decodePNG/measureLuma, and reproduces every published r15 figure to the digit before reporting anything — specks meanRGB 54.9,43,36.8; specks p1/p50/p99 18.6/44.8/75.1; bare meanRGB 41,32.3,27.1; farright lumaSpread 44.9; frame p01/p1/p99 12/18/196; pctBelow16 0.458; pctAbove240 0.005; p50 92; whole-frame saturation 0.2322 against the critic's 0.232.

APPARATUS FAILURE, recorded so the next round does not repeat it: the first ablation attempt copied tools/_abl-materials.mjs's deterministic A/B pattern (engine.stop, reset TAA and _adaptReset, one pipeline.render(0)). All eight configs came back byte-identical in every probe box at p50 4 with 98.716% of the frame under luma 16 — a uniform ~1/12 scaling. _passAdapt writes the adaptation target that the NEXT composite reads, so a single reset frame composites against the pre-reset value, and nothing recomposited afterwards. The rig now leaves the engine running and settles like capture.mjs, hashes every shot, and flags any config byte-identical to base. That pattern is safe for a single A/B toggle inside one already-adapted frame; it is not safe for a multi-config sweep.

unresolvedQuestions: Target (d), at least one plateau sample box returning G > R. The classification is NOT the obstacle and that is the round's most useful negative result: run offline through the real pipeline, the visible plateau is 57.8% grass before this change and 57.2% after, and the 'grass' layer samples the moss library texture (PAL.mossDeep #2f4426, moss #4e6b3c, mossDry #7c8a4e, linear G/R 2.04/1.93/1.26) tinted (0.44,0.50,0.26), so its albedo G/R is about 2.1. Yet across the whole frame only 336 of 2,730 64x64 tiles measure G > R and every one of them is sky; inside the critic's plateau box the best tile reaches G/R 0.900 and the median is 0.780. The green is therefore lost downstream of classification. The three candidate terms, all in the 0.3-7 m dressing, are cStraw applied at up*0.80 (warm and about 2.8x the luminance of the turf it replaces), cTurf diluted 72% toward a near-neutral (0.10,0.13,0.15), and the litter drift mixing colGravel*(1.18,0.86,0.47) at lit*0.60 on a 3.9:1 wind-elongated field — which is also the best candidate for the finding's 'obvious stretching along one axis'. The ablation built to separate them (tools/_abl-world.mjs, configs nodress / splat-grass / nodress-grass) was still queued behind four other owners' rigs when this record was written. It was NOT acted on unmeasured, per the standing rule.
Whether the foliage owner's instanced cover on the wide plain lands in the same 40-90 m band, in which case targets (c) and (d) are joint and neither owner's number is separable.

valley already measures saturation 0.609 against a 0.55 target. The mid band's dry/damp tints are close to balanced in B/R (mean ln(B/R) shift about -0.02) so the predicted move is under 0.01, but it is in the wrong direction.

The splat grid is 3.2 m at MEDIUM, so the new 2.7 m-wide worn route is roughly one texel and renders as a soft 3-6 m band rather than a crisp track. At 50 m that is ~20-30 review pixels and reads as a path; on a nearer framing it would not.

acceptanceCriteriaNotes: PREDICTION, target (c): farright box (2152,702,304x117) lumaSpread rises from 44.9 to >= 70. Modelled at 91 before tone-map compression from sigma_log 0.2755 -> 0.4694 stops; the shoulder takes the top off it. The critic's >= 80 is inside the model and outside the conservative bound, and the gap is where the foliage owner's instanced cover would land.

PREDICTION, target (c) second-order: the same box's `detail` moves little. detail is a 1-pixel Laplacian and kgMidBand is ~12 drawing-buffer pixels (22 review pixels) by construction, so predict detail 4.98 -> 5.2-6.5, not a large move. Anyone reading a flat detail number as a failed fix will be reading the wrong metric.

PREDICTION, target (a) partial: whole-frame p1 18 -> 12-15 and pctBelow16 0.458% -> 0.9-1.5% from Terrain alone. p1 <= 8 and pctBelow16 >= 3.0% are not reachable from this file (disproof above). Whole-frame p50 must stay inside 92.8 +/- 10; the mid band is debiased in stops so its own contribution to p50 is designed to be zero.

PREDICTION, target (b): whole-frame saturation 0.232 -> at most about 0.255 from Terrain alone, against the 0.29 target. The dry and damp tints are near-balanced in B/R by construction; whole-frame saturation is an illuminant property and belongs to Lighting.js.
